documents.unit: Office of the Provost and Division of Student Affairs
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy Reminder (letter to students)
documents.summary: A 2023 letter from the Provost and the Dean of Students reminding students that the existing academic integrity policy bars unauthorized assistance, which covers generative AI unless an instructor permits it. It sends students to their syllabi, their instructors and Computing Services guidance.
documents.stance_why: The letter says the integrity policy "prohibits 'unauthorized assistance,' which would include generative AI tools unless explicitly permitted by the instructor". AI is therefore banned unless an instructor permits it, which is restrict, although the permission is left to instructors.

units.why: The letter says the existing integrity policy "prohibits 'unauthorized assistance,' which would include generative AI tools unless explicitly permitted by the instructor". That is a default ban with instructor permission as the exception, so it is the fallback rule (P06) and not P01, because permission is left to each instructor.
units.anchor: prohibits "unauthorized assistance," which would include generative AI tools unless explicitly permitted by the instructor

units.why: "Carefully review your course syllabi to understand what is and is not acceptable in each of your courses" says the rule is set course by course in syllabi, so it is per-instructor rule setting (P04). It does not fit P10 because it is not about asking when unsure.
units.anchor: Carefully review your course syllabi to understand what is and is not acceptable in each
units.frag_end: using generative AI tools in your coursework

units.why: "Talk to your instructors if you have questions about these policies or syllabi" is advice to ask the instructor when unsure, which is P10.
units.anchor: Talk to your instructors if you have questions about these policies or syllabi

units.frag_end: adhering to our highest academic standards

units.why: The letter points students to "Computing Services' Generative Artificial Intelligence Guidelines and Guidelines for Data Classification" for best practices. This refers to university data and tool guidance, so P50.
units.anchor: Refer to Computing Services’ Generative Artificial Intelligence Guidelines and Guidelines for Data Classification

units.why: The letter states the goal "to address their challenges and lean into the opportunities" by "ensuring you have clear guidance and expectations". It states the purpose and principle of the institutional approach, so P56.

documents.title: Examples of possible academic integrity policies that address student use of generative AI tools
tiers: No generative AI in any form
Generative AI fully encouraged with citation
Generative AI allowed in some cases but not others
documents.summary: The teaching center offers six sample syllabus statements: two banning AI, two encouraging it with citation and verification, and two allowing it only for named assignments or class exercises. Each is a template that instructors adapt.
documents.stance_why: The page says the examples "represent a range of options one could adapt or adopt", with six statements from full ban to full encouragement. It sets no stance of its own and hands the choice to instructors, so delegates, with the three kinds of statement listed as tiers.

units.why: The preface says the examples are "a range of options one could adapt or adopt", a menu of alternative policy positions for instructors. That is a set of named options (P05) addressed to instructors, not itself a rule on AI.
units.anchor: The following examples represent a range of options one could adapt or adopt
